validity.researcher_notes: EXISTENCE overwhelmingly confirmed by sources with zero GEM lineage: FERC's own Federal Register notices (govinfo.gov FR-1997-11-13 'Destin Pipeline Company, L.L.C. and Southern Natural Gas Company; Notice of Availability of the Final Environmental Impact Statement for the Proposed Destin Pipeline Project', docket CP96-655-001 et al.; federalregister.gov 2002/04/12 02-8899 'Destin Pipeline Company, L.L.C.; Notice of Application' re Pascagoula Gas Plant modifications; and a separate FERC Order 63, docket CP04-371-000, naming 'Destin Pipeline Company, L.L.C.' as one of Chandeleur's three downstream interconnects), Enbridge's current corporate factsheet, an SEC EDGAR exhibit (American Midstream Partners, LP EX-99.5, 2016), Natural Gas Intelligence coverage spanning 2000-2016, Rextag's pipeline database, Oil & Gas Journal (1998), and Wikipedia. This is a real, currently-operating FERC-jurisdictional interstate gas transmission/gathering pipeline. CLASSIFICATION (gas pipeline, operating) is correct and consistent across every source -- Destin functions as a hybrid offshore-gathering/onshore-interstate-transmission system per its own operator's description, matching how comparable Gulf systems in this roster (Chandeleur P0165, Nautilus, Garden Banks) are classified. DUPLICATE CHECK against the 50-row Gulf-Coast roster: no other row represents this physical corridor -- Destin's Gulf of Mexico (Main Pass area) to Pascagoula/Moss Point, MS route is geographically distinct from Chandeleur (also terminates at Pascagoula but via a separate, independently FERC-certificated system, docket CP04-371), Garden Banks, Nautilus, Sea Robin, Independence Trail, and Mississippi Canyon; no merge/relabel indicated. The 120-mile offshore portion of the Destin system terminates at the Pascagoula processing plant'); (5) Rextag's pipeline database ('Destin Pipeline, a 255-mile pipeline running from the Gulf of Mexico to the Pascagoula processing plant'). A sixth, historical data point (Oil & Gas Journal, 1998-06-29, mid-construction) describes 'the 214-mile Destin pipeline project' -- a still-different figure from a still-earlier project phase, further evidence 385 has never been documented for this system. gem.wiki's own infobox (385 mi, citing the Enbridge factsheet) is directly contradicted by its own prose paragraph below the infobox, which states 'The pipeline's 255-mile length includes a 120-mile offshore portion... 135 miles north' -- i.e. GEM's own page disagrees with itself, and the live source it cites for 385 does not currently say that. Did NOT stage a Length [ref] fill supporting the current 385.00 mi value. Recommend Baird review and correct to 255 mi if independently agreed, rather than the agent silently overwriting a value column.

validity.researcher_notes: This is the known issue flagged for this row: sheet StartState/Province reads 'Mississippi' but the route starts offshore. NGI (2000-03-06) identifies Destin's offshore mainline hub platform as 'Main Pass Block 260' ('The 36-inch offshore mainline runs 76 miles from Main Pass Block 260 to the Pascagoula Gas Plant'). Main Pass is a BOEM/BSEE Gulf of Mexico OCS protraction area consistently attributed to Louisiana, not Mississippi, across every independent institutional source checked: NOAA IncidentNews labels an incident 'Main Pass Block 299; Offshore, LA' (incidentnews.noaa.gov/incident/6055); BSEE's own unit-agreement filing for Main Pass Block 299 is titled 'MAIN PASS BLOCK 299 UNIT AGREEMENT OFFSHORE, LOUISIANA'; and general descriptions place Main Pass 'south of the Louisiana coastline.' I did not find a source stating 'Main Pass Block 260, Louisiana' verbatim (only block 299 and 6 were directly confirmed in institutional records this pass), so this stays medium tier rather than high -- it is a strong, consistent naming-convention inference, not a block-260-specific document. Zero sources found attributing any Main Pass block to Mississippi. EndState/Province='Mississippi' is independently confirmed correct and unrelated to this concern: the 2002 Federal Register notice (federalregister.gov 02-8899) states Destin's Pascagoula Gas Plant is 'located in Jackson County, Mississippi', matching Enbridge/NGI/Rextag/SEC's consistent description of the onshore terminus. Recommend Baird confirm before changing StartState/Province given the block-260 caveat.

summary: Existence/classification/duplicate all confirmed via sources with zero GEM lineage (FERC Federal Register notices across three separate dockets, Enbridge's current factsheet, an SEC EDGAR exhibit, NGI 2000/2016, Rextag, OGJ 1998, Wikipedia). Staged REFS_ADDED for 8 of 9 MISSING_REF cells at high-to-medium tier (Status/Fuel/Capacity/Diameter/Operator/Owner high; Start/Construction medium, single-origin but second-source search documented) plus a filled Proposal (1996, medium). TWO material concerns flagged rather than rubber-stamped: (1) spec -- LengthKnown=385mi is contradicted by FIVE independent sources (including Enbridge's own current factsheet, the very document gem.wiki cites) all agreeing on 255mi; not staged as confirmed. (2) attribution -- StartState/Province='Mississippi' is likely wrong per the task's own flagged known issue; Destin's offshore hub is Main Pass Block 260, and Main Pass is conventionally Louisiana OCS territory (NOAA/BSEE), though a block-260-specific document was not found, so this stays medium tier. A third concern flags SegmentCost=$386M as unverifiable (its only lineage is a non-citable EIA navigation page; the one dollar figure independently found, $460M, is a bundled pipeline+gas-plant cost, not a segment figure). Pressure/FuelSource/SegmentCost left UNRESOLVED with documented searches, consistent with the FuelSource gotcha in gem_schema.md (Destin gathers from multiple offshore platforms, no single named source). No duplicate or classification concerns; no cross-row leads warranted new routing (the one candidate lead, P0199/Gulfstream, already has independently well-sourced Diameter/Length in this same batch).
